chunks: 3269 - And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated, saying:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A Jewish or Christian man had four thousand dirhams with me, then he died. Is it permissible for me to reach a settlement with his heirs without informing them how much it was?
He عليه السلام said: “It is not permissible until you inform them.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: four thousand dirhams owed as a financial amount
key_terms.أُصَالِحَ: to make a settlement or compromise

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to settle a debt with a deceased person’s heirs without telling them the full amount owed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on financial rights owed to the heirs of a deceased non-Muslim. It establishes that one may not settle for less or conceal the true amount of a debt; the heirs must first be fully informed so that their rights are preserved.
